advice: Recommend one limited n=512 experiment: keep the existing ZA transpose and FP32 SME outer-product arithmetic, but add cache blocking only to the output column loop. Process adjacent column tiles in small groups while reusing each loaded A vector across those tiles; retain the current general path for other n and all tails. This is a hypothesis about reuse, not evidence of a cache bottleneck or a predicted gain. Supplied results do not isolate cache effects or establish a stable candidate gain.
risks: Extra live ZA accumulators or vectors can raise register pressure and reduce throughput; changing tile scheduling can also add loop overhead. Avoid proposing a specific block size as established without measurements. Check correctness against the fixed tolerance on n=512, odd dimensions, small positive n, and n<=0; then compare with a fresh AC baseline using repeated paired controls under the unchanged hill and settings. Attribute any result only to the tested candidate, not an advisor.
